claims.claim: Intersect's Technical Steering Committee requests $298,250, stated as 1,193,000 ADA, to support TSC activities for 12 months.
The proposal allocates 256,000 ADA to WP1, 832,000 ADA to WP2, and 105,000 ADA to WP3, totaling 1,193,000 ADA.
WP2 will fund three specialist groups: the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group.
WP3 will establish a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027, with conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal states that all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and links to voting documentation and audited results.
The requested amount is stated not to breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission, with a link to the referenced governance action.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible review of deliverables, controls, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

Intersect will use a Sundae Labs treasury management smart contract framework with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, defined multi-party authorization thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for tracking funds.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of TSC support through Intersect, with three budgeted work packages, smart-contract-based fund administration, audit/oversight commitments, NCL compliance claims, and referenced Hydra voting and smart contract materials.
